problem: Given that $y=2{x}^{3}-2x$ for $x=x(t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=1$ at the point where $x=-2,$ find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-5x \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-5x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-5x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (-3{x}^{2}+8x-5).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-3$ and $x=2,$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =(-3)\cdot (-3\cdot (2)^{2}+8\cdot (2)-5)=3.\end{aligned}
$$
